text: Hello, everyone.Nice to see you again.I'm Sarah.Welcome to my class again.In today's lesson, you will continue the grammar section and you will listen to something interesting.In the story Nobody Wins, when all the crew were caught in the cage by the Master Gorg, there was a dialogue between the crew.Do you remember who said the sentence and to whom?It's Lam.Who said this to Captain King?Chloe, can you read the sentence aloud?You were wrong about the monster being friendly, weren't you?Good pronunciation.What does this sentence mean?Who thought the monster was friendly?Captain King did.Was Captain King right or wrong about this?He was wrong.So what did Lam suggest by saying this sentence?She wanted the captain to agree that he was mistaken.Another question.Is this sentence a statement or a question?Look, I've changed Lam's remark a little bit.Here I've got four sentences.Read them and tell the difference.The first sentence is a simple statement.成數據 From the sentence, we know that Captain King was wrong about Gorg being friendly.And the speaker is quite sure about that.The second sentence is a yes-no question.一般疑問句 It really asks the question whether Captain King was wrong or not.The expected answer is either yes or no, or words that mean yes or no.The third one is a rhetorical question.反問句 It shows that Lam knew King was wrong and she wanted to emphasize King's wrong judgment.If Lam says such a sentence to Captain King, who has a higher position, she will sound very rude.This question doesn't expect an answer.The last sentence is what Lam said in a story.This sentence is actually made up of two parts.A statement and a short question.The short question at the end of the sentence is called question tag or tag question.And when we write, there is a comma before the question tag.The whole sentence still ends with a question mark.We use question tags in spoken English and in informal written English.Let's look at more examples to see how question tags are formed.Can you work out the rules for yourselves?What rules can you come up with?Victoria, please.If the statement is positive, we use a negative question tag.If the statement is negative, we use a positive question tag.Good.The two parts opposite rule.The positive-negative or negative-positive structure.What else, Jason?Question tags consist of a helping verb and a pronoun.Right.Question tags are made up of a helping verb.For example, did, was, have, could, and a subject pronoun.For example, he, she, it.They are in short form.What about the tenses?Daniel?The verbs in the tag must have the same tense as the verb in the statement sentence.Brilliant.You figured out the forms for yourselves.Then, how can we answer these questions?Often, we just say yes or no according to the truth of the situation.Your answer reflects real facts.For example, Peters was lost again, wasn't he?The answer should be yes, he was.It means Peters was lost.What about this sentence?Gork gave a rule, didn't he?Flora, can you answer it?Yes, he did.That's right.And how would you answer this question?Lem didn't trust Captain Kin, did she?Did Lem trust Captain Kin till then?No, she didn't.The fact is that Lem didn't trust Captain Kin.So the answer should be no, she didn't.Can you answer these two questions?Captain Kin could save them, couldn't he?And King's plan wasn't a good one, was it?I'm afraid I will leave the questions for you to answer after you finished reading the whole story.Question tags are not difficult, are they?But almost every grammar rule has some special cases.Now let's read more sentences.These three statements are positive or negative imperatives.其始句 Usually we use will you as the question tag.Look at the last sentence.This imperative begins with let's.We should use shall we as the question tag.We found some other exceptions in the question tag.Look at these sentences.We should use there in a question tag when the sentence begins with there be.How can we add a question tag to this statement?We should say, could they?The words nobody, never, rarely, seldom and hardly have a negative sense.We treat statements with these words as negative statements.So the question tag is normally positive.Here are more examples for you.Now it's your turn to have a try.Can you correct the mistakes in the following question tags?This is task one on your worksheet.This is task two.Can you correct the mistakes in the following questions?This is task three.How is it going?Let's check the answers.Obviously, these mistakes are easy to find, aren't they?Now we know how question tags are formed.But when and why do we use them?Let's review Lam's words again.Previously, we explained that by saying this, Lam warned the captain Kin to agree that he was wrong.Since Captain Kin has a higher position than she, Lam used a question tag to make herself sound less rude.So, we often use question tags when we expect the listener to agree with our statements.In this case, it is not really a question.We are simply making a statement.Another example, one of the popular greetings.It is a lovely day, isn't it?We are simply making a statement and we are looking for agreement.Let's read the second sentence.Who said this?Captain Kin.Why did he say this?He was asking if Peters could find the way.He was checking if this was true.He wasn't sure about that.The question tag here is used to check if the statement is true.This is another way of asking a question.We could just ask a Could Peters find a way?Let's do some practice.You will find it on your worksheet.Task 2.Match the sentence with its meaning.Ready?Here are the possible answers for your reference.I say possible answers instead of correct answers.Why do I say so?That's because sometimes the intonation the speaker uses will change the meaning.Let me read the same sentence twice, but in different tones.Listen to me carefully.Peters didn't know Captain King's plan.Did he?Can you hear any differences?Claudie?You use a rising tone for the first sentence and a falling tone for the second one.You are quick-eared.When we read a sentence in a rising tone, did he?It is a real question.Our voice goes up.We want to find whether the statement is true or not.The question expects an answer or reply.When we read a sentence in a falling tone, did he?The question itself is not a real question.Here we know the answer.We are just checking information and we expect the listener to agree.Now, can you read these sentences without changing their meanings?Peter, will you have a try?I also enclosed a photo of our school.It is beautiful, isn't it?The meeting is at ten o'clock, isn't it?Your name is Peters, isn't it?Yesterday was so much fun, wasn't it?Gork has never been to the earth, has he?Peter sounds like a native speaker, doesn't he?I think so.What would your answer be?I would say no, he never has.But here is a piece of breaking news.Recently, a newspaper called Earth Daily reported about a visitor from outer space.Who is it?Look at the picture.As the title suggests, a visitor from outer space.Is it Gork?A reporter accidentally took a photo of the visitor.This one is a lady with long hair.She looks so similar to Gork, also with a single huge red eye.What is the possible relationship between her and Gork?Yvonne?Maybe they are husband and wife.And you, Tony?Maybe she is Gork's daughter or his mother.Interesting gases.She looks younger.Maybe she is Gork's sister.Let's name her Gorkella.In the story Nobody Wins, we've learned Gork is an unfriendly and cruel monster.What about his sister?Why did he come to the earth?Jerry?Maybe she wanted to go sightseeing.What's your view, Amy?Maybe she wanted to make friends with human beings because she was waving her hand to us in the photo.It seems that she is not that horrible.There are many possibilities.She must have her plan.Where did she land?Can you find any clues in the picture?Janice?I think she landed in Shanghai because I can see the Oriental Pearl TV Tower.I agree.The Oriental Pearl TV Tower is one of the most famous and beautiful scenic spots in Shanghai.Today, we are going to learn about Gorkella's visit to Shanghai.Since Shanghai is an interesting city, where do you think Gorkella might go if she wants to visit Shanghai?Kelly?She can go to Nanjing Road, The Bund and Yu Garden.These places are very beautiful, especially at night.Right, these places are in the city center.Where else, Jason?She can have fun in some parks like Changfen Park and Zhongshan Park.Good idea.What about you, Daniel?She can go to the Oriental Pearl TV Tower and Shanghai Disney Resort.They are in Pudong, the other side of the Huangpu River.But where did Gorkella actually go?Take a close look at the pictures and read the words.Can you spot the places?You can see the Oriental Pearl TV Tower, Hopping Restaurant and Nanjing Road in the pictures.Now, open your student's book and turn to page 100.Listen to the report and number the pictures.Picture 1Gorkella wanted to visit China.She flew her spaceship over Shanghai and landed next to the Oriental Pearl TV Tower.Picture 2Gorkella got out of her spaceship and decided to cross the river.She took the Pujang ferry.She sat on the roof so that she could enjoy the view.Picture 3She then walked around the streets, looking at the shops.Unfortunately, she walked on some of the cars.Picture 4Next, she went to Changfeng Park.It was a hot day, so Gorkella had a swim in the lake.Picture 5After her swim, Gorkella was hungry.She went to a restaurant and had a seafood meal.She ate all of the fish.Picture 6She then walked over to Jiangshan Park.She was feeling tired, so she sat down on a big piece of wood.It then went down the steps very fast.Picture 7Gorkella decided that it was time to go home.She took the underground back to the Oriental Pearl TV Tower.The other passengers stood far away from the doors when she got out.Picture 8Lots of people were angry with Gorkella because she had broken lots of things.Finally, she got into her spaceship and flew home.Have you put the pictures in the right order?Time, please.I think the order should be 6, 7, 8, 4, 5, 1, 3, 2.You've got a correct answer.What an amazing visitor.She went to so many different places.What did she do there?Let's listen again and filling the table with right words and phrases.This is task 3 on a worksheet.Let's check the answers in complete sentences.Aria, have a try.Gorkella landed next to the Oriental Pearl TV Tower.She took the Pujian ferry to cross the river and sat on the roof to enjoy the view.Then, she walked around the streets, looking at the shops and even walked on some of the cars.She had a swim in the lake in Changfeng Park.Well done, Aria.What did she do in other places?Kelly, please.She had a seafood meal and ate all of the fish in the seafood restaurant.In Zhongshan Park, she sat down on a big piece of wood and the wood went down steps very fast.She went to an underground station and took the underground back to the Oriental Pearl TV Tower.At last, she got into her spaceship near the Oriental Pearl TV Tower and flew home.Good job, Kelly.Gorkella had a great fun in our city.But how do you think the people around felt about her?And how did people react?Look at pictures again.Yuki, what do you think?In the restaurant and Zhongshan Park, people felt scared and ran away from Gorkella quickly.People waiting on the underground station stayed far away from her for fear of getting hurt.And lots of people were angry with her because she had broken lots of things.Excellent.Thank you, Yuki.Gorkella's visit to Shanghai seemed to cause a stir.A reporter from Earth Daily wants to interview some witnesses,目记者, who saw Gorkella in different places.Suppose you are the reporter.What questions will you ask the witnesses?You can use question tags to confirm information or look for agreement.Yvonne, what's your question?You saw the alien next to the Oriental Pearl TV Tower, didn't you?Ryan, suppose you are one of the witnesses.How would you respond?Yes
